stops.text: 04:30, Midway time. Before sunrise the Kidō Butai turns into the south-easterly breeze and launches its strike on Midway: level bombers, dive bombers and fighters from every carrier. Far to the east, unseen, the American carriers wait for news.
05:52. A Catalina finds the carriers, steaming south-east, and reports them; the American carriers hear it and turn to close.

06:34. Midway’s guns are firing; bombs fall on the seaplane hangars and fuel tanks of Sand Island and on Eastern Island’s buildings. The runways are left almost untouched. Midway’s own fighters have already met the strike, thirty miles out, and few of them come back.

07:10. Midway’s torpedo planes and Army bombers come in low from ahead. Akagi swings hard and combs the torpedoes; the fighters overhead cut the attackers down. At 07:15 Vice Admiral NAGUMO Chūichi 南雲忠一 orders his second wave re-armed with bombs for Midway.

07:28. Tone’s search plane, launched late, reports enemy ships to the north-east. Vice Admiral NAGUMO Chūichi 南雲忠一 reverses his order at 07:45: the planes still carrying torpedoes keep them. Through the morning Midway’s dive bombers and B-17s attack and hit nothing.

09:20. Torpedo Eight, without fighters, finds the carriers and attacks alone, low under the cloud. The combat air patrol meets it eight miles out and follows it all the way in. None of its aircraft return.

tellings.says: All 15 TBDs lost; one pilot, Ensign Gay, survived in the water.

stops.text: 09:40. Torpedo Six attacks Kaga from both bows; the carriers turn away to hold the torpedo planes on the quarter, and the fighters come down to meet them.
10:09. Torpedo Three and its handful of fighters come in from the south-east. The Zeros are low over them, and the sky above the carriers is empty.
10:22. Enterprise’s dive bombers fall on Kaga out of the scattered cumulus. Yorktown’s Bombing Three is pushing over on Sōryū; three of Enterprise’s go north to Akagi.
10:26. Within minutes Kaga, Sōryū and Akagi are burning, the fuelled and armed aircraft in their hangars feeding the fires. Hiryū, further north, is untouched.
10:54. Hiryū launches her dive bombers against the American carriers while Rear Admiral ABE Hiroaki 阿部弘毅 signals that the other three are burning.
12:05. Yorktown’s fighters break up Hiryū’s dive bombers well out, but some get through. Three bombs hit; a hit in the uptakes stops her.
14:44. Hiryū’s torpedo planes come in from both sides through the screen’s fire. Two torpedoes hit Yorktown’s port side; she loses power and lists, and is abandoned half an hour later.
17:03. Dive bombers from Enterprise, Yorktown’s among them, find Hiryū with the low sun behind them. Her helm throws off the first; then bombs strike forward.

17:55. The day ends with every carrier of the Kidō Butai burning. Kaga and Sōryū sink in the evening; Akagi and Hiryū are scuttled by their own destroyers the next morning. Yorktown is afloat and abandoned; a submarine’s torpedoes sink her on 7 June.

moments.title: Bombing Six pushes over on Kaga

Hits aft and at the forward elevator.

record.note: Bombing Six’s share of the hits on Kaga is inferred (see the 10:22:40 event); the whole attack put three to five bombs on her

after.text: Nagumo’s report has the first bombs missing and four striking Kaga, one of them on the bridge. Fires spread through her hangars among armed and fuelled aircraft. She burned through the afternoon and sank at 19:25. Many of Enterprise’s dive bombers came down at sea on the way home, their tanks empty.

tellings.says: Bombs 4, 7, 8 and 9 hit; Kaga’s dead printed “1 800” (garbled).

VS-6 and VB-6 lost seven aircraft each that morning; four and possibly as many as seven ditched for want of fuel.

moments.title: Three Dauntlesses turn north to Akagi

role.name: a Dauntless of Bombing Six’s leading section

objective.text: Dive on Akagi and put your bomb on her flight deck.

beats.text: Akagi swings into a hard reverse turn below you.
The first bomb bursts close aboard her bridge.
Fire in Akagi’s upper hangar.

checkpoints.text: Akagi is burning; the torpedoes in her hangar begin to go off.

after.text: One bomb, probably Lieutenant Richard H. Best’s, burst among the armed and fuelled aircraft in Akagi’s upper hangar. A near miss astern jammed her rudder. By 10:42 her engines had stopped; Vice Admiral NAGUMO Chūichi 南雲忠一 left her, and she was scuttled at dawn on 5 June.

tellings.says: Two hits and a near miss; 221 of her crew lost their lives.

moments.title: Bombing Three dives on Sōryū out of the sun

A third amidships; the last of the squadron turn on a destroyer and a battleship.

checkpoints.text: Sōryū is burning end to end.

after.text: Three bombs hit Sōryū. Within a quarter of an hour her engines had stopped and her steering had failed, and at 10:45 her captain ordered her abandoned. She sank at 19:13. None of Bombing Three was lost over the target.

tellings.says: 718 of her crew lost their lives.

record.note: what the record gives the combat air patrol over Torpedo Three: ten of twelve lost, seven before the drop, no torpedo hit

after.text: Hiryū’s fighters claimed nearly every torpedo plane and every escort. The record has most of Torpedo Three lost and one of its escorts; Hiryū combed the torpedoes and was not hit. At 10:22, while the fighters were low in the south-east, dive bombers fell on Kaga, Akagi and Sōryū.

tellings.says: Claimed: nine of fourteen torpedo planes, all nine fighters.
Yorktown lost 10 of 12 torpedo planes.
The Japanese brought most, if not all, of the defending fighters down to low altitudes, leaving few if any to oppose the dive bombers.
After Parshall and Tully: a failure of control and position; a Zero could regain 10,000 ft in about five minutes.

objective.text: Keep the Zeros off the torpedo planes below you.

beats.text: Zeros come down on the rear of the formation.
Two bursts of flak mark you for the fighters.

checkpoints.text: The torpedo planes press on through the fighters.

after.text: Six Wildcats fought far more Zeros over Torpedo Three, weaving in pairs. One was lost; another crash-landed on Hornet. Torpedo Three pressed its attack and most of its aircraft did not return.

tellings.says: VF-3 counted 15 to 20 Zeros; one F4F lost, five or six Zeros claimed.

One at a time, bombers break away toward the carrier.
A bomb bursts on Yorktown’s flight deck aft.

after.text: A few of Hiryū’s dive bombers got through to Yorktown and three bombs hit; one in her uptakes stopped her. Most of the bombers and some of their fighters did not return; Lieutenant (大尉) KOBAYASHI Michio 小林道雄 was among them. Hiryū reported the carrier sunk; within an hour and a half Yorktown was steaming again at nearly twenty knots.

tellings.says: 13 of 18 bombers and 3 fighters did not return.
Seven broke through; three hits.

after.text: The combat air patrol broke up the attack fifteen to twenty miles out; a few bombers got through and three bombs hit Yorktown. The fighters claimed most of the bombers; the Japanese record agrees nearly to the aircraft. Many of the Wildcats had run out of ammunition before the attack was over.

tellings.says: Claimed: thirteen bombers and two fighters.

after.text: Hiryū’s torpedo planes split to come in from both sides; two torpedoes hit Yorktown. Half of them did not return, among them the aircraft of Lieutenant (大尉) TOMONAGA Jōichi 友永丈市. Hiryū believed she had disabled a second carrier. Yorktown was abandoned within half an hour and sank on 7 June after a submarine’s torpedoes.

tellings.says: 5 of 10 torpedo planes lost, with 3 escorts.
Five launched; the last two, released at about 800 yards, hit at 1445.

role.name: a Dauntless of Enterprise’s afternoon strike

objective.text: Dive on Hiryū out of the low sun.

Bombs strike Hiryū forward.

after.text: Four bombs hit Hiryū, three in a row forward and one by the bridge. She burned all night. Rear Admiral YAMAGUCHI Tamon 山口多聞 and Captain KAKU Tomeo 加来止男 stayed aboard when she was scuttled the next morning. Some of the dive bombers did not return.

tellings.says: 416 of her crew lost their lives.
417, counting 34 engine-room men later rescued by US forces.
Three did not return.
Japanese dead about 2,500; 234 carrier aircraft lost (48 shot down, 186 lost aboard or ditched). US dead about 307; 132 aircraft lost.
After Parshall and Tully: 3,057 Japanese lost their lives, and 248 aircraft were lost (verify).
About 92 officers and 215 men lost; about 150 planes lost in action or damaged beyond repair.
